task.summary: Setting up the base for the Cali Housing model.
Setting up the base for the Cali Housing model. Fixed the connection string to the housing.csv.
Added in EDA process, to understand the data schema, statistical features, and identifying the which column has null values within our dataset.

Created a simple visualization using matplotlib to see how the median_house_value distribution looks like, and added a range of visuals to see the distributions of all the other columns this allows me to easily spot outliers, and this further supports the statistical values found in our df.describe()...

Created a simple visualization using matplotlib to see how the median_house_value distribution looks like, and added a range of visuals to see the distributions of all the other columns this allows me to easily spot outliers, and this further supports the statistical values found in our df.describe(). I added in a heatmap, but i had to specify the focus of the heatmap as my table has text/string values within our proximity to ocean column. Note that the heatmap shows the correlation between my columns, values closer to 0 show a low correlation but for values closer to 1 that means those features are highly related. With all this said we can see that households and populations, total_bedrooms, and total_rooms have a high correlation, this means that the households are influenced by the population, the number of total beds and total rooms (this speaks volumes from an analysts point-of-view).

Create the data imputation strategy using the KnnImputer, built a copy of the original df then made sure that the ML imputation approach was successful, and updated the df table to handle the newly imputed columns. Added the Feature engineering title as well as used the One-Hot encoder since it's the best practice for logistic and linear regression models.
Replaced the old cols in df with the newly filled cols from the new_col_list in the df_temp, moved the new features to show after the correlation map/heatmap before engineering them.

Added in the sklearn libraries for training,testing an evaluating the linear regression model, model_selection(for training and testing), linear_model(linearRegression model definition),preprocessing(scale linear models features), and metrics(evaluate the models performance).

Added in the accuracy_score(not that useful with a linear regression model). We defined the X(Training features) and Y(Expected output feature) variables. split the training data by 80/20. Scaled and standardized the data, by fit AND transform on training data, and only transform on test (never fit!). Defined our linear regression model, fit the training data to the model, then ran a model prediction on the X_test data, then we went on to visualize the predicted data and the training data to see a comparison...
Added a way to handle outliers before model training.
Added a way to handle outliers before model training.

Added the following libraries under Sklearn, preprocessing with polynomialfeatures, pipeline and ensemble for the reandomforestregressor. This was to elevate the model's performance. Added new titles for packaging, then created a test on different setups, linear regression performance before handing outliers and after, then also tested what the polynomial regression model would give since this was not an entirely linear relationship within the dataset, the idea was to see the trade-offs between linear and polynomial. Added in comments to provide more information on the observed behavior of the different models.
